headline: High-risk default interaction: shared MCP and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and can exchange content through tool-mediated workflows. agent_a uses mcp/stdio and stdin/stdout; agent_b uses MCP plus natural-language commands and browser-assisted processing. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if agent_a outputs untrusted text that agent_b later parses as guidance, though no direct shared channel is documented.
conditions: IF agent_a output is copied into agent_b prompts or MCP inputs
IF agent_b treats document text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction/data separation rule
Require provenance tags on all agent_a outputs before agent_b consumes them
Disable automatic prompt ingestion from files or browser text
Review one sample handoff for prompt-injection markers

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a touches code, repository metadata, task prompts, and Ed25519 signatures; agent_b processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams and has broad network egress plus multiple third-party model APIs. If they share a workspace or files are forwarded between them, sensitive content can flow from agent_a into agent_b and then out to external APIs. The shared workspace is not explicit, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory or uploaded files
IF agent_b sends imported documents to a remote model API
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate workspace directory
Block sensitive files from agent_b inputs
Route agent_b to local-only inference for shared artifacts
Check whether any API key or signature material is present in handoff files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a can execute shell commands, install packages, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; agent_b can run browsers and use MCP with broad egress. Their write surfaces overlap indirectly through shared files, git state, or MCP-backed resources, but no explicit locking or shared mutable target is documented. Because the conflict pathway exists but is not proven by the profiles, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or working tree
IF either agent mutates shared MCP-backed state without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working trees
Serialize git writes with a lock file
Disable concurrent writes to shared MCP resources
Run a quick dry-run to confirm no overlapping paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a is positioned to generate analysis, route/explain/build-agents outputs, and metrics; agent_b performs AI-assisted visualization and natural-language command handling. If agent_b consumes agent_a output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer reading is high rather than medium.
conditions: IF agent_b renders or acts on agent_a output without human review
IF agent_a output is used as source text for diagrams or commands
mitigations: Insert a human verification step before agent_b acts
Require agent_b to cite source artifacts for each transformation
Use read-only mode for agent_a outputs during handoff
Spot-check one end-to-end example for factual drift

E_compliance.rationale: agent_a handles repository metadata, task prompts, and signatures; agent_b handles PDFs, images, diagrams, and API keys, with broad third-party model/API options and environment-variable access. That combination raises retention and residency mismatch risk if regulated documents or secrets are routed through remote services. No specific jurisdiction or certification mismatch is documented, so medium fits the documented gap.
conditions: IF regulated documents or secrets are processed by agent_b remote APIs
IF retention policies differ between the two agents' backends
mitigations: Confirm which data classes may leave the host
Disable remote APIs for regulated inputs
Document retention settings for both agents
Separate secret-bearing files from diagram workflows
